question: ​Amylopectin is a branched-chain polysaccharide composed primarily of glucose units linked by____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**α-1,4-Glycosidic bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amylopectin** is a highly branched polysaccharide primarily composed of **glucose units**. It is one of the two main components of starch, the other being amylose.
 
• Amylopectin primarily consists of glucose units linked by **α-1,4-Glycosidic bonds** in the linear chains. These bonds occur between the first carbon of one glucose molecule and the fourth carbon of the next molecule.
 
• In addition to α-1,4-Glycosidic bonds, amylopectin has branching points formed by **α-1,6-Glycosidic bonds**. These branches occur roughly every 24–30 glucose units. However, the correct answer specifically refers to the primary linkage, which is the α-1,4-Glycosidic bond.
 
• Amylopectin is insoluble in water compared to amylose, and its branched structure makes it easier to break down during digestion. This is due to the accessibility of enzymes like amylase to the branching points.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is α-1,4-Glycosidic bond.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Amylopectin:**

 
 
• **Amylopectin** is a branched polymer of glucose and constitutes approximately 70–80% of starch.
 
• The branches in amylopectin are created by **α-1,6-Glycosidic bonds**, which contribute to its highly branched structure.
 
• The linear chains of glucose are connected by **α-1,4-Glycosidic bonds**, forming the backbone of the molecule.
 
 
 
• **Function and Importance:**
 
 
• Amylopectin serves as an **energy storage molecule** in plants. When starch is broken down, glucose units are released for metabolic processes.
 
• **Enzymatic digestion:** Amylopectin is hydrolyzed by enzymes such as amylase, which target the α-1,4 and α-1,6 linkages.
 
• The branched structure of amylopectin allows rapid mobilization of glucose during metabolic needs.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Amylose:**
 
 
• **Amylose** consists of linear chains of glucose molecules linked by α-1,4-Glycosidic bonds. It is less branched and more compact compared to amylopectin.
 
• Amylose is more resistant to digestion due to its linear structure, whereas amylopectin is more easily digested.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **α-1,4-Glycosidic Bond:**

 
 
• This bond is a type of covalent bond formed between the first carbon atom (C1) of one glucose molecule and the fourth carbon atom (C4) of another glucose molecule.
 
• It is crucial for the formation of polysaccharides like amylopectin and amylose.
 
 
 
• **α-1,6-Glycosidic Bond:**
 
 
• This bond forms the branching points in amylopectin. These branches allow enzymes to act more efficiently, aiding in digestion and energy release.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Amylopectin is widely used in food industries for its thickening and stabilizing properties.
 
• It also plays a role in the production of bioethanol and other biochemicals due to its glucose content.
